narrative_prose: Kaio bounded across the jagged basalt outcroppings, his brass sextant catching the surreal glow of the twin suns as they dipped low. Before him lay the ferrofluid sea, an alien expanse of dark metallic liquid that didn't just ripple—it sheared. The magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz instability tore at the boundary layer, throwing up sharp, shifting spikes of iron-rich fluid. He paused, whistling a three-note tune as he charted the chaotic flow, knowing that a single misstep into the resonant spore-fog would mean disaster. The tension in the air was electric, biting at his exposed skin. He had to map this corridor for The Sanctuary, to understand how the currents twisted the local gravity. It wasn't about fighting the current, but finding the rhythm of its violence. A sudden spike of magnetic pressure warned him of a rising wave. He adjusted his stance, shielding his instruments from the spray. With the final measurements locked in, he grinned through the ozone-scented air. Turning back to the ridgeline, he saw Ryn approaching. Kaio jogged over, clapping Ryn on the shoulder, and passed over the glowing, ozone-scented sextant, the baton officially handed off.
